name: Mass estimator: fresh validation grid for prior factors, dominance and switch rules

aims: Provide fresh observations on the operating-range grid to validate conclusions first drawn from the 21 September operating-range archive: where the ratio of means beats every archived point rule, how two-branch switch rules compare with it, and whether a sech-tilt prior parameter fitted on that archive keeps its worst-case regret reduction.
No estimator, parameter or score is tuned on these observations. The fitted parameter is frozen before this study is analyzed.
data_generating_mechanisms: Newton II is assumed correct. One compatible latent 3D pair per replicate; common direction is used only by the simulator and remains unknown to inference.

Known independent isotropic Gaussian coordinate SD 1 in both channels, one effective reading per channel, R=10000 replicates per cell with fresh seeds. The same replicate-index noise is shared across cells; cells cannot be pooled as independent evidence.
Effective force and acceleration SNRs cross [1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16] (64 cells), identical to the operating-range protocol; only the seeds differ.
estimands: Per cell and tolerance factor K in {1.25,1.5,2}: probability that a positive estimate lies in [m/K,K*m], all attempted trials included.
Per cell: paired failure differences between point rules on identical replicates, and regret against the best archived rule.
methods: Existing isotropic comparison engine unchanged; all eleven archived point rules and posterior summaries are saved.

Prior-weighted laws, switch rules and dominance classifications are computed afterwards from the saved observations and points by prior_weight_study.py, switch_rules.py and paired_dominance.py; nothing is refitted or discarded.
performance_measures: Paired MCSE is the sample SD of the paired difference over sqrt(R). Classifications use a two-sided Bonferroni normal bound over the declared family, stated in each analysis output.
Report only sampled cells; do not infer an observed-data rule from a truth-indexed map.

methodology.title: Morris, White and Crowther: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
Gneiting: Making and Evaluating Point Forecasts

interpretation: Designed after exploratory analysis of the operating-range archive on 23 September 2026; this study supplies fresh draws for that follow-up, not independent discovery.
Every result is conditional on the declared Gaussian isotropic known-noise model and one effective reading per channel.
